{{inline |date=May 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''nilpotent cone''' <math>\mathcal{N}</math> of a finite-dimensional [[semisimple Lie algebra]] <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> is the set of elements that act nilpotently in all [[representation of Lie algebras|representations]] of  <math>\mathfrak{g}.</math> In other words,  

:<math> \mathcal{N}=\{ a\in \mathfrak{g}: \rho(a) \mbox{ is nilpotent for all representations } \rho:\mathfrak{g}\to \operatorname{End}(V)\}. </math>

The nilpotent cone is an [[algebraic variety|irreducible subvariety]] of  <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> (considered as a [[vector space]]).

==Example==
The nilpotent cone of <math>\operatorname{sl}_2</math>, the Lie algebra of 2×2 [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]] with vanishing [[trace (linear algebra)|trace]], is the variety of all 2×2 traceless matrices with [[rank (linear algebra)|rank]] less than or equal to <math>1.</math>
